As I look back at Trent’s journey, I am filled with a deep
sense of reflection. What started as a thoughtful transition
from Lakmé into an emerging fashion retail space has, over
time, become something ever more meaningful.
On a personal note, I often reflect on the early conversations
I had with my mother, Mrs. Simone Tata, when we were
considering the transition of Lakmé into a new direction. At
the heart of those discussions was a simple but powerful
aspiration - to create products and experiences that people
truly love and desire and yet rooted in Tata values. It is
deeply satisfying to see that, in many ways, this aspiration
has come to fruition through Trent’s progress over the past
two and a half decades.
In 1998, when we began with a single Westside store at
Commercial Street in Bengaluru, modern fashion retail in
India was almost non-existent. The idea of creating a
contemporary, accessible retail experience for Indian
consumers was both ambitious and uncertain. Yet, it was
also energising - because we were not just building a
business, we were participating in shaping a new business
category in the country.
More than 25 years later, the transformation has been
extraordinary - first and foremost for India itself. The India
we operate in today is vastly different. There is a greater
exposure to global trends, rising aspirations across
demographics, and an increasing ability among consumers
to pursue lifestyle choices. The growth in disposable
incomes and the desire for self-expression through fashion
have fundamentally reshaped consumption patterns.
We have witnessed a remarkable evolution - not only in
people’s sense of fashion, but also in how they think,
choose, and live. The proliferation of choice, the openness
to change, and the confidence of the Indian consumer
have all contributed to creating a vibrant and
competitive marketplace.
Through all these changes, I am extremely proud that Trent
has remained grounded and anchored firmly in the values
of the Tata group. Even as the environment became more
Dear Shareholders,
dynamic and competitive, and even as consumer
expectations underwent dramatic shifts, our focus on
delivering genuine customer value has remained
unwavering.
From a single Westside store to a network of over twelve
hundred stores, our journey has been one of steady
evolution. Over the years, we have added powerful growth
engines to our portfolio - most notably Zudio and Star -
which are now a significant part of our portfolio. The
strength of Trent today lies not just in scale, but in the
diversity and relevance of our brands.
We have also worked towards building an integrated
ecosystem - across design, sourcing, supply chain, and
retail execution - to ensure that each of our brands delivers
a differentiated and compelling customer experience. This
ability to combine back-end strength with front-end
innovation has been central to our progress.
I have long believed that Trent is not intended to be defined
by a single brand, but rather by a portfolio of brands. In a
diverse and evolving market like India as well as globally, it
is unlikely that any one brand can capture a dominant share
of the lifestyle space. Instead, our approach has been to
create distinct, well-defined propositions that cater to
different customer needs and occasions. This multi-brand
strategy will continue to guide our future.
As we look ahead, I firmly believe that the best years of
Trent are ahead of us. The opportunities before us are vast -
not just in India. In the years to come, I see Trent touching
even more lives through our offerings, expanding across
categories, and exploring new geographies
over time.
It would be enormously satisfying to shape and build
brands from India that go on to be globally relevant in
diverse markets. Further, as we consider this future, we
should also aspire for material scale of revenues from
overseas markets. This would be completely in line with the
national agenda of growing value added exports from our
country. We should aspire boldly, execute with
perseverance and celebrate the pride of brands - built
ground up from India!
As we move forward, our journey will remain deeply
collaborative. Our stakeholders - our employees, partners,
suppliers, communities, and shareholders - are integral to
everything we do. Together, we will continue to build a
responsible, sustainable, and meaningful business of scale.
Given the significant opportunities that remain ahead and
the growing strength of Trent’s platform, I believe we are still
at an early phase of our growth journey. With a strong
ecosystem around us and a clear sense of purpose, we are
positioned to build upon this platform.
In our 2023 shareholders meeting, I had envisioned Trent to
be ten times bigger in terms of revenues with
commensurate profitability. Since then, the revenue and
profitability run rate has grown by over 2.5 times. Given all
this, I am confident that we will reach the milestone I had
referenced in the not-so-distant future.
I sincerely thank you for your continued trust in Trent and for
being an integral part of our journey.

Risk Governance
The Risk Management Committee, the Audit Committee, and the Board review
periodic updates on key enterprise risks and material changes in the Company’s
risk profile, ensuring effective oversight at the highest levels. The execution of
the risk management framework is driven by a central Risk Management function
under the leadership of the Chief Financial Officer, enabling a consistent and
coordinated approach across the organisation. The Company has adopted
the COSO 2017 Enterprise Risk Management Framework for driving its risk
management agenda. Ongoing communication initiatives and structured risk
workshops promote awareness, accountability, and transparency in risk reporting.
The use of technology and advanced analytics supports efficient, accurate, and
timely monitoring of risks.

Board Meetings:
Board Meetings are conducted in a structured and
timely manner at regular intervals to review strategy,
business updates, financial performance, operational
matters, risk management, governance and compliance
matters, etc.
The Board Meeting frequency is decided in accordance
with the applicable statutory requirements to ensure
effective governance and continuous oversight of
the Company’s operations. Additional Meetings are
convened as necessary to address any other urgent or
significant decisions.
During FY 2025-26, the Board met 5 times i.e. on
29th April 2025, 6th August 2025, 7th November 2025,
4th February 2026 and 26th March 2026.
The Board Meetings were held as per the prescribed
timelines and gap between two Board Meetings did
not exceed 120 days. The Meetings were conducted
in compliance with all the applicable laws and the
necessary quorum was present for all the Meetings.
Board Procedure:
The Board and Committee Meetings are scheduled
well in advance at the beginning of the year to enable
effective planning and participation. Agenda papers
and supporting documents are shared with Directors
through a secure digital platform sufficiently ahead
of the Meetings, allowing easy access. Directors may
seek clarifications through the Company Secretary, as
required. This helps for productive discussions and
informed decision-making at the Board Meetings.
The Board during the Meetings reviews the business,
operational, financial and governance matters of the
Company and its key subsidiaries. To support effective
oversight, the Managing Director provides periodic
business and operational updates, with members
of the senior leadership team attending Meetings
as necessary. The Chairpersons of the respective
Committees periodically brief the Board on significant
deliberations, recommendations and outcomes of
Committee Meetings.
The Chairman encourages open and constructive
discussions, ensuring active participation, independent
views and healthy challenge to Management.
Minutes of the Board Meetings capture discussions and
decisions taken at these Meetings. Actionable items
are systematically tracked and reviewed in subsequent
Meetings, thereby reinforcing strong oversight,
accountability and alignment with the Company’s
governance objectives.
Term of the Board:
In accordance with the Tata Group guidelines adopted
by the Company, the retirement age prescribed for
Executive Directors is 65 years, for Non-Independent
Non-Executive Directors is 70 years and for Independent
Directors is 75 years.
The composition of the Board ensures that at least
two-third of the total Board members (excluding
Independent Directors) are subject to retirement by
rotation, with at least one-third retiring at each AGM.
Executive Directors are appointed for a tenure not
exceeding five years, as prescribed under the Act
and by their service contracts with the Company.
Non-Executive Directors (excluding Independent
Directors) are subject to retirement by rotation as per
the provisions of the Act and if eligible, may get re-
appointed at the AGM.
Independent Directors are appointed for a term of up
to five years and are eligible for re-appointment for an
additional term.
The Chairman of the Board is not liable for retirement by
rotation; however, his appointment is subject to approval
of the Shareholders once in every five years as per the
SEBI Listing Regulations.

• Store L&D Strategy
The store L&D framework is structured around three pillars - functional training, behavioural training and leadership

Timely and regular safety training is essential for minimizing workplace accidents and ensuring employee well-being.
These sessions provide valuable insights into their working environment, potential hazards and effective prevention
measures. As a critical component of the identification and management of workplace risks, all employees undergo
Health and Safety training as part of the induction process upon joining the Company. Additionally, they are trained to
use the Safety Reporting System to raise timely alerts about unsafe conditions through iSafe, the Company’s Incident
Reporting application.
Moreover, the Company’s associates are regularly trained to ensure they understand the process and importance of
reporting all incidents and injuries to the Health and Safety team. This proactive approach helps to prevent unsafe
behavior, address unsafe conditions in the workplace and reduce the likelihood of occurrence of adverse incidents.
Key safety training programs provided to employees include Women’s Safety Training, Two-Wheeler Safety Training
and Fire & First Aid Safety Training. In addition, stores colleagues are assigned periodic H&S training modules through
Trent’s various e-learning platforms Seekho (Westside), Zlearn (Zudio) and SuccessFactors (for offices and other
locations). Employees are also imparted training on the Tata Group’s Accelerated Reduction in Repeat Events (‘ARRE’)
initiative, which enhances H&S awareness and promotes continuous improvement. Our focus areas include air quality
monitoring, water quality testing, ergonomics review, quarterly servicing of air conditioning filters, and ensuring that
workplace illumination levels consistently meet or exceed compliance standards.
